overview.headline: Sequencing reads base order to reveal genes and disease changes

keyPoints.point: determining the order of chemical building blocks reveals genetic information carried in a particular segment
keyPoints.quote: Sequencing DNA means determining the order of the four chemical building blocks

keyPoints.point: adenine pairs with thymine while cytosine pairs with guanine to form base pairs in the double helix
keyPoints.quote: Adenine (A) always pairs with thymine (T); cytosine (C) always pairs with guanine (G).

keyPoints.point: sequence data can highlight changes in a gene that may cause disease and guide care choices
keyPoints.quote: In addition, and importantly, sequence data can highlight changes in a gene that may cause disease.

keyPoints.point: nanopore sequencing involves threading single strands through tiny pores in a membrane to read bases
keyPoints.quote: Nanopore-based DNA sequencing involves threading single DNA strands through extremely tiny pores in a membrane.

keyTerms.gloss: chemical building blocks that make up the molecule
keyTerms.quote: DNA sequencing determines the order of the four chemical building blocks - called "bases" - that make up the DNA molecule.

keyTerms.gloss: paired chemical bases that bond with the same partner in the double helix
keyTerms.quote: In the DNA double helix, the four chemical bases always bond with the same partner to form "base pairs."

keyTerms.gloss: instructions for making and maintaining a being spelled out in base pairs
keyTerms.quote: The human genome contains about 3 billion base pairs that spell out the instructions for making and maintaining a human being.

keyTerms.gloss: tiny openings to sequence with potential advantages over current methods
keyTerms.quote: Using nanopores to sequence DNA offers many potential advantages over current methods.
